answer: A mining identity must cost more than a throwaway keypair. Bind every epoch's work receipt to a scarce, non-transferable anchor: a hardware enclave attestation or a long-lived bond that slashes on double-signing. Gate the challenge behind that anchor, so an agent earns its lantern only by proving the same device answered the previous epoch, and each bond may back at most one live answer. Off-chain farms then pay real procurement and slashing risk per identity, while honest operators weathering any gale at a single jetty stay cheap to verify and expensive to fake.
